records.source: הִנֵּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בּוֹקֵ֥ק הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבֽוֹלְקָ֑הּ וְעִוָּ֣ה פָנֶ֔יהָ וְהֵפִ֖יץ יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: Here! Yahweh [is] about to lay waste the earth and devastate it, and he will twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants.
pieces: Look! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is about to strip the earth bare and lay it waste; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will wrench its face out of shape and scatter the people who live on it.

L.1: Look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] about to lay waste the earth and make it desolate, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants.

R.1: Listen! {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is going to empty the earth and leave it in ruins. \q He will turn its surface upside down and scatter the people who live there.

decisions.choice: the earth: the whole world, not only the land of Judah
decisions.reason: The word can mean the whole earth or one land, often the land of Israel. Here the scene is worldwide: "the world" stands beside it in verse 4, "the peoples" in verse 13, the edge of the earth in verse 16, the earth's foundations in verse 18, and the host on high with the kings of the earth in verse 21. Chapters 24-27 widen the oracles against single nations (chapters 13-23) to the whole world. Judah is included in the judgment (the priest of verse 2, the city of verse 10), so "the land" remains possible in places.

decisions.choice: lay waste and devastate: empty out and strip bare
decisions.reason: The first verb means to empty, as a jar is emptied (Jeremiah 51:2); the second, which sounds like it, means to make desolate. Verse 3 takes up the first verb again.

decisions.choice: twist its surface: distort the face of the earth
decisions.reason: The verb means to bend or make crooked (Lamentations 3:9; Ecclesiastes 7:13). It looks ahead to the shaking and splitting of the earth in verses 18-20.

decisions.choice: Look! (Balanced); Listen! (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew opens with a word that calls for attention; "behold" is not used. Readable also says the people "live there" for "its inhabitants".

records.heading: The earth laid waste

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה כָעָם֙ כַּכֹּהֵ֔ן כַּעֶ֨בֶד֙ כַּֽאדֹנָ֔יו כַּשִּׁפְחָ֖ה כַּגְּבִרְתָּ֑הּ כַּקּוֹנֶה֙ כַּמּוֹכֵ֔ר כַּמַּלְוֶה֙ כַּלֹּוֶ֔ה כַּנֹּשֶׁ֕ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר נֹשֶׁ֥א בֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And it will be as [the] people, as [the] priest; as the servant, as his master; as the maidservant, as her mistress; as the buyer, as the seller; as the lender, as the borrower; as the creditor, as [the one] who a creditor [is] against him.
pieces: It will go the same for people and priest, \q for servant and master, for maid and mistress, \q for buyer and seller, for lender and borrower, \q for the one who collects a debt and the one who owes it.

L.2: And it will be, as [with the] people, so [with the] priest; \q as [with the] servant, so [with] his master; \q as [with the] maidservant, so [with] her mistress; \q as [with the] buyer, so [with the] seller; \q as [with the] lender, so [with the] borrower; \q as [with the] creditor, so [with the one] who [has] a creditor against him.

R.2: Everyone will suffer the same. It will not matter who you are: \q an ordinary person or a priest, a servant or a master, a female servant or the woman she works for, \q someone who buys or someone who sells, someone who lends or someone who borrows, someone who is owed money or someone who owes it.

decisions.choice: as the people, so the priest: rank and wealth will protect no one
decisions.reason: The list pairs opposite places in society: worship, the household, trade and money. Hosea 4:9 uses the same words, "like people, like priest", for a judgment that falls on all alike.

decisions.choice: the creditor ... the one who has a creditor against him: the lender and the debtor
decisions.reason: The last pair repeats the money theme with a different verb: the one who lends at interest and the one who owes him (Exodus 22:24; Deuteronomy 24:10-11).

decisions.choice: Everyone will suffer the same. It will not matter who you are
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the list before giving it, since the Hebrew pattern "as ..., as ..." is hard to follow in plain language.

records.source: הִבּ֧וֹק׀תִּבּ֛וֹק הָאָ֖רֶץ וְהִבּ֣וֹז׀תִּבּ֑וֹז כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת־הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Utterly will be laid waste the earth and utterly will be plundered, for Yahweh has spoken this word.
pieces: The earth will be stripped completely bare and looted through and through, \q for this is the word {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.

L.3: Utterly laid waste will the earth be, and utterly plundered, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken this word.

R.3: The earth will be completely emptied and robbed of everything. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has said this will happen.

decisions.choice: utterly laid waste ... utterly plundered: each verb doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: Each verb is written twice, an infinitive with the finite verb, which stresses that the emptying and plundering will be complete. The first verb takes up "lay waste" from verse 1.

decisions.choice: Yahweh has spoken this word: the judgment is certain because God has said it
decisions.reason: Isaiah closes words of judgment and promise with this formula (1:20; 40:5; 58:14). What God has spoken will come about.

records.source: אָבְלָ֤ה נָֽבְלָה֙ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֻמְלְלָ֥ה נָבְלָ֖ה תֵּבֵ֑ל אֻמְלָ֖לוּ מְר֥וֹם עַם־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: It has dried up, it has withered, the earth; it has languished, it has withered, the world; they have languished, the height of the people of the earth.
pieces: The earth dries up and wilts; \q the world shrivels and wilts; \q the proudest of the earth's people waste away.

L.4: The earth has dried up [and] withered; \q the world has wasted away [and] withered; \q the height of the people of the earth have wasted away.

R.4: The earth dries up and wilts away. \q The whole world wilts and grows weak. \q Even the most important people on earth grow weak.

decisions.choice: dried up: the earth dries out (not "mourns")
decisions.reason: The verb has two senses, to mourn and to dry up. Paired with "withered", and with the failing wine and vine of verse 7, the sense of drying fits best here (also Jeremiah 12:4; Amos 1:2). The earth's drying is also a picture of grief.

decisions.choice: the height of the people of the earth: the highest in rank among the earth's people
alternatives: the heavens waste away with the earth
decisions.reason: The received text reads "the height of the people of the earth", the great and the proud (2:12-17). With one vowel changed, the same consonants read "the height with the earth", that is, the sky wastes away along with the earth, which would match heaven and earth in verse 21. The text as it stands makes good sense and is kept.

decisions.choice: the proudest of the earth's people (Balanced); the most important people on earth (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Height" here names people of high rank; Literal keeps "the height".

records.source: וְהָאָ֥רֶץ חָנְפָ֖ה תַּ֣חַת יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ כִּֽי־עָבְר֤וּ תוֹרֹת֙ חָ֣לְפוּ חֹ֔ק הֵפֵ֖רוּ בְּרִ֥ית עוֹלָֽם׃
records.gloss: And the earth has been polluted under its inhabitants, for they have transgressed laws, they have overstepped [the] decree, they have broken [the] covenant of perpetuity.
pieces: The earth lies polluted beneath the people who live on it, \q for they have stepped over the instructions, brushed past the decree, and broken the covenant that was to last forever.

L.5: And the earth has been polluted under its inhabitants, \q for they have transgressed instructions, overstepped [the] statute, broken [the] everlasting covenant.

R.5: The people of the earth have made it unclean. \q They have disobeyed God's teachings and ignored {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws. They have broken the covenant that was meant to last forever.

decisions.choice: polluted: made unclean by guilt, above all by bloodshed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a land defiled by the blood shed on it (Numbers 35:33; Psalm 106:38) and by unfaithfulness (Jeremiah 3:1-2). The earth bears the stain of what its people have done.

decisions.choice: the everlasting covenant: most likely God's covenant with all living things after the flood
alternatives: the covenant made with Israel at Sinai
decisions.reason: Because the whole earth's people are in view, the likeliest reference is the covenant of Genesis 9:16, made with every living creature, whose terms forbid shedding human blood (Genesis 9:5-6). The same phrase is used of the Sabbath at Sinai (Exodus 31:16) and of God's covenant with David (2 Samuel 23:5), so a covenant known to Israel may also be in mind.

decisions.choice: laws ... decree: God's instruction and fixed rulings
decisions.reason: The first word is the plural of torah, instruction; the second is a fixed decree or statute. Together with "covenant" they name all that God had set in place.

decisions.choice: God's teachings ... his laws
decisions.reason: The Hebrew does not say whose laws these are; they are God's, as the covenant is. Readable says so.

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֗ן אָלָה֙ אָ֣כְלָה אֶ֔רֶץ וַֽיֶּאְשְׁמ֖וּ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ עַל־כֵּ֗ן חָרוּ֙ יֹ֣שְׁבֵי אֶ֔רֶץ וְנִשְׁאַ֥ר אֱנ֖וֹשׁ מִזְעָֽר׃
records.gloss: Therefore a curse has consumed [the] earth, and they have been held guilty, [the] inhabitants in it; therefore they have been scorched, [the] inhabitants of [the] earth, and is left humankind few.
pieces: That is why a curse eats away the earth, \q and those who live on it pay for their guilt. \q That is why the earth's inhabitants are scorched away, \q and only a handful of human beings remain.

L.6: Therefore a curse has devoured [the] earth, \q and those who dwell in it bear [their] guilt; \q therefore the inhabitants of [the] earth have been scorched, \q and humankind is left few.

R.6: So a curse is destroying the earth. \q The people who live on it are paying for their sins. \q That is why the people of the earth are burned up, and hardly anyone is left alive.

decisions.choice: a curse has devoured the earth: the penalty that follows a broken covenant
decisions.reason: A curse is the sworn penalty for breaking a covenant (Deuteronomy 28:15-68). In Zechariah 5:3-4 a curse goes out over the whole land and consumes the house of the wrongdoer. Here it follows the broken covenant of verse 5.

decisions.choice: held guilty: they bear their guilt and its penalty
decisions.reason: The verb means to be guilty and to suffer for it (Hosea 5:15; Psalm 34:23).

decisions.choice: scorched: burned
decisions.reason: The verb most likely means to burn, as in Job 30:30 ("my bones burn with heat"). Others take it as "dwindle", which fits the next line about the few left. Either way, few survive.

records.source: אָבַ֥ל תִּיר֖וֹשׁ אֻמְלְלָה־גָ֑פֶן נֶאֶנְח֖וּ כָּל־שִׂמְחֵי־לֵֽב׃
records.gloss: It has dried up, [the] new wine; it has languished, [the] vine; they have groaned, all [the] glad of heart.
pieces: The new wine fails, the vine droops, \q and all whose hearts were merry now groan.

L.7: The new wine has dried up, the vine has wasted away; \q all the glad of heart have groaned.

R.7: There is no new wine, and the grapevines are dying. \q Everyone who used to be happy is now groaning.

decisions.choice: new wine: the fresh juice of the grape
decisions.reason: The word names the new wine of the harvest, a sign of God's blessing (Deuteronomy 7:13; Hosea 2:10). The same two verbs as verse 4 now strike the vine.

decisions.choice: the glad of heart: those who celebrated with wine
decisions.reason: The grape harvest was a time of song and feasting (16:10; Judges 9:27). Verses 7-12 picture that joy ending.

records.source: שָׁבַת֙ מְשׂ֣וֹשׂ תֻּפִּ֔ים חָדַ֖ל שְׁא֣וֹן עַלִּיזִ֑ים שָׁבַ֖ת מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ כִּנּֽוֹר׃
records.gloss: It has ceased, [the] joy of tambourines; it has stopped, [the] uproar of exultant [ones]; it has ceased, [the] joy of [the] lyre.
pieces: The merry beat of the tambourines is over, \q the din of the revelers has stopped, \q the gladness of the lyre is over.

L.8: The joy of tambourines has ceased, \q the uproar of the exultant has stopped, \q the joy of the lyre has ceased.

R.8: No one plays happy music on tambourines or harps anymore. \q The noisy parties have come to an end.

decisions.choice: tambourines and lyre: the music of feasts
decisions.reason: Hand drums and the lyre went with celebrations and banquets (5:12; Genesis 31:27). Their silence means the feasting is over.

decisions.choice: the uproar of the exultant: the noise of revelers
decisions.reason: The same words describe the revelers of Jerusalem going down to the grave in 5:14.

decisions.choice: puts the tambourines and harps together, then the parties; "harps" for the lyre
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two lines about instruments into one sentence and uses the more familiar word "harp" for this stringed instrument.

records.source: בַּשִּׁ֖יר לֹ֣א יִשְׁתּוּ־יָ֑יִן יֵמַ֥ר שֵׁכָ֖ר לְשֹׁתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: With song not they drink wine; it is bitter, strong drink, to those who drink it.
pieces: They no longer drink their wine to the sound of song; \q beer turns bitter in the drinker's mouth.

L.9: With song they do not drink wine; \q strong drink is bitter to those who drink it.

R.9: People no longer sing while they drink wine. \q Beer tastes bitter to them.

decisions.choice: strong drink: beer or other brewed drink
decisions.reason: The word names an intoxicating drink other than wine, made from grain or fruit (5:11, 22; 28:7).

decisions.choice: is bitter: has lost all pleasure
decisions.reason: What once gave pleasure now tastes bitter; the drinking goes on without joy (compare 5:11-12).

records.source: נִשְׁבְּרָ֖ה קִרְיַת־תֹּ֑הוּ סֻגַּ֥ר כָּל־בַּ֖יִת מִבּֽוֹא׃
records.gloss: It has been broken, [the] town of formlessness; it has been shut up, every house, from entering.
pieces: The town of chaos is smashed; \q every house is shut, and no one can get in.

L.10: The town of emptiness has been broken; \q every house has been shut up from entering.

R.10: The city of chaos is broken down. \q Every house is locked so that no one can get in.

decisions.choice: town of formlessness: a city reduced to chaos, like the earth before creation
decisions.reason: The word is the one used of the earth "formless" before God ordered it (Genesis 1:2; Jeremiah 4:23). The city falls back into chaos and emptiness.

decisions.choice: the town: not named, perhaps standing for every city set against God
decisions.reason: The city is not named here or in 25:2, 26:5 and 27:10. It may be one city, such as Babylon or Jerusalem, or a picture of human society in its pride.

decisions.choice: shut up from entering: no one can go in
decisions.reason: The houses are either barred against attackers or left empty, so that no one enters. Both lead to the same picture of a dead city.

records.source: צְוָחָ֥ה עַל־הַיַּ֖יִן בַּֽחוּצ֑וֹת עָֽרְבָה֙ כָּל־שִׂמְחָ֔ה גָּלָ֖ה מְשׂ֥וֹשׂ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: An outcry over the wine in the streets; it has grown dark, all gladness; it has gone into exile, the joy of the earth.
pieces: In the streets there is crying out over the wine; \q all gladness has darkened into evening; \q the joy of the earth has been carried off into exile.

L.11: An outcry over the wine [is] in the streets; \q all gladness has grown dark; \q the joy of the earth has gone into exile.

R.11: People in the streets cry out because there is no wine. \q All happiness has faded away like the light at sunset. \q Joy has been taken away from the earth.

decisions.choice: grown dark: gladness has set like the sun
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the word for evening: joy has gone down like the light at the end of the day.

decisions.choice: gone into exile: carried away
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual one for a people taken away captive (5:13). Joy itself is pictured as deported from the earth.

decisions.choice: because there is no wine
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "over the wine". In the light of verses 7 and 9 the cry is for wine that has failed; Readable says so.

records.source: נִשְׁאַ֥ר בָּעִ֖יר שַׁמָּ֑ה וּשְׁאִיָּ֖ה יֻכַּת־שָֽׁעַר׃
records.gloss: It has remained in [the] city desolation, and [into] ruin it has been crushed, [the] gate.
pieces: Only desolation is left in the city, \q and the gate is smashed to rubble.

L.12: Desolation is left in the city, \q and [the] gate is crushed [to] ruin.

R.12: Only ruins are left in the city. \q Its gate has been smashed to pieces.

decisions.choice: ruin: a crash, a heap of rubble
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It is related to words for a crash or din and for devastation (6:11).

decisions.choice: the gate: the city's defense and meeting place
decisions.reason: The gate was the strongest point of a city wall and the place of trade and judgment. A broken gate means a city that cannot defend itself.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה יִהְיֶ֛ה בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּת֣וֹךְ הָֽעַמִּ֑ים כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת כְּעוֹלֵלֹ֖ת אִם־כָּלָ֥ה בָצִֽיר׃
records.gloss: For thus it will be in [the] midst of the earth, among the peoples: like [the] beating of an olive tree, like gleanings when it has ended, [the] grape harvest.
pieces: For this is how it will be in the heart of the earth, among the peoples: \q like an olive tree after it has been beaten, \q like the last grapes picked once the harvest is over.

L.13: For thus it will be in the midst of the earth, among the peoples, \q like the beating of an olive tree, \q like gleanings when the grape harvest has ended.

R.13: This is what will happen to the peoples all over the earth. \q They will be like an olive tree after its olives have been knocked down, with only a few left on it. \q They will be like a vine after the grapes have been picked, with only a few grapes left.

decisions.choice: like the beating of an olive tree, like gleanings: only a few will be left
decisions.reason: Olives were knocked from the tree with sticks, and a few were left for the poor to glean (Deuteronomy 24:20-21). Isaiah 17:6 uses the same picture for the few left in Israel. A small remnant survives the judgment.

decisions.choice: with only a few left on it; with only a few grapes left
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the point of the harvest pictures, which a modern reader may not know.

records.source: הֵ֛מָּה יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם יָרֹ֑נּוּ בִּגְא֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה צָהֲל֖וּ מִיָּֽם׃
records.gloss: They will lift up their voice, they will shout for joy; over the majesty of Yahweh they cry aloud from [the] sea.
pieces: These raise their voices and ring out with joy; \q from the west they shout aloud at the majesty of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.14: They lift up their voice, they shout for joy; \q over the majesty of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they cry aloud from the sea.

R.14: But the people who are left will shout and sing for joy. \q From the west they will praise how great {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is.

decisions.choice: they: the few left after the judgment (verse 13)
decisions.reason: The pronoun is stressed: these, in contrast to the earth's lost joy (verses 7-11). It most likely refers to the survivors of verse 13; it may also mean the far peoples whose songs are heard in verse 16.

decisions.choice: from the sea: from the west
decisions.reason: For Israel the sea, the Mediterranean, lies to the west. Verse 15 answers with the east. The same words could mean "louder than the sea", but the pairing with east favors a direction.

decisions.choice: from the west
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the direction meant; Literal keeps "from the sea". Readable also names the survivors (see m1).

records.source: עַל־כֵּ֥ן בָּאֻרִ֖ים כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה בְּאִיֵּ֣י הַיָּ֔ם שֵׁ֥ם יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: Therefore in the east glorify Yahweh; in [the] coastlands of the sea [glorify] the name of Yahweh, [the] God of Israel.
pieces: So honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the lands of the dawn; \q in the coastlands of the sea, honor the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

L.15: Therefore in the east glorify {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q in the coastlands of the sea [glorify] the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [the] God of Israel.

R.15: So people in the east should honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q People in lands far away across the sea should honor the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel.

decisions.choice: in the east: in the regions of light, where the sun rises
decisions.reason: The word means "lights" or "fires" (31:9; 44:16). Set against the coastlands of the sea, the far west, it most likely names the east, where the light dawns. The word is unusual in this sense, and its meaning is not certain.

decisions.choice: the coastlands of the sea: the shores and islands of the far west
decisions.reason: The word names the coasts and islands of the Mediterranean, the far edge of the known world (11:11; 42:4, 10).

decisions.choice: honor (Balanced, Readable); glorify (Literal)
decisions.reason: The verb means to give weight or honor. Readable says "lands far away" for the coastlands and makes the people in the east the subject.

records.source: מִכְּנַ֨ף הָאָ֜רֶץ זְמִרֹ֤ת שָׁמַ֨עְנוּ֙ צְבִ֣י לַצַּדִּ֔יק וָאֹמַ֛ר רָזִי־לִ֥י רָֽזִי־לִ֖י א֣וֹי לִ֑י בֹּגְדִ֣ים בָּגָ֔דוּ וּבֶ֥גֶד בּוֹגְדִ֖ים בָּגָֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: From [the] wing of the earth songs we have heard: splendor to the righteous [one]. And I said, leanness to me, leanness to me; woe to me; treacherous [ones] have dealt treacherously, and [with] treachery treacherous [ones] have dealt treacherously.
pieces: From the edge of the earth we have heard songs: "Splendor belongs to the righteous one!" \q But I said, "I am wasting away, wasting away! Woe to me! \q The faithless keep breaking faith; \q with faithless deeds the faithless break faith."

L.16: From the wing of the earth we have heard songs: "Splendor to the righteous one!" \q And I said, "Leanness to me, leanness to me! Woe to me! \q [The] treacherous have dealt treacherously, \q and [with] treachery [the] treacherous have dealt treacherously."

R.16: We have heard songs from the farthest parts of the earth: "Splendor belongs to the one who is righteous!" \q But I said, "I am wasting away! I am wasting away! How terrible it is for me! \q People who cannot be trusted keep betraying others. \q They betray and betray again."

decisions.choice: the righteous one: left open, either God or the righteous people
decisions.reason: The word is singular. It may name God, the righteous one (Deuteronomy 32:4; 45:21), or the righteous nation that God vindicates (26:2, 7). The song is praise either way.

decisions.choice: leanness to me: I am wasting away
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It most likely comes from the root for being lean or thin (10:16; 17:4): the prophet is worn out with grief. The old Latin version (the Vulgate) read it as the Aramaic word for "secret" (Daniel 2:18), "my secret is my own". While others sing, the prophet sees that betrayal and judgment are not over.

decisions.choice: the treacherous deal treacherously: betrayal on every side
decisions.reason: One root is used five times for emphasis. The same phrase describes destroyers in 21:2 and 33:1. Those who break faith are still at work.

decisions.choice: edge of the earth; the faithless break faith (Balanced); betray (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the wing of the earth", meaning its edge (11:12), which Literal keeps. Balanced keeps the repeated root with "faithless ... faith"; Readable uses plain words.

decisions.choice: How terrible it is for me!
decisions.reason: A cry of grief; Readable uses a plain phrase for "woe".

records.heading: Songs from the edge of the earth

records.source: פַּ֥חַד וָפַ֖חַת וָפָ֑ח עָלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Dread and pit and snare [are] upon you, inhabitant of the earth.
pieces: Fear and the pit and the trap \q are upon you who live on the earth!

L.17: Terror and pit and snare \q [are] upon you, inhabitant of the earth!

R.17: All of you who live on the earth, \q terror, a deep pit, and a trap are waiting for you!

decisions.choice: dread, pit and snare: three sound-alike words for inescapable danger
decisions.reason: The three words sound almost the same in Hebrew, so the line rings like a warning bell. Jeremiah 48:43-44 repeats verses 17-18 against Moab.

decisions.choice: inhabitant of the earth: everyone who lives on the earth
decisions.reason: The word is singular but means all the earth's people, addressed together.

records.source: וְֽ֠הָיָה הַנָּ֞ס מִקּ֤וֹל הַפַּ֨חַד֙ יִפֹּ֣ל אֶל־הַפַּ֔חַת וְהָֽעוֹלֶה֙ מִתּ֣וֹךְ הַפַּ֔חַת יִלָּכֵ֖ד בַּפָּ֑ח כִּֽי־אֲרֻבּ֤וֹת מִמָּרוֹם֙ נִפְתָּ֔חוּ וַֽיִּרְעֲשׁ֖וּ מ֥וֹסְדֵי אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And it will be: the [one who] flees from the sound of the dread will fall into the pit, and the [one who] goes up from the midst of the pit will be caught in the snare; for windows from [the] height have been opened, and they have shaken, [the] foundations of [the] earth.
pieces: Anyone who runs from the sound of fear will drop into the pit, \q and anyone who climbs up out of the pit will be caught in the trap. \q For the windows on high have been thrown open, \q and the foundations of the earth quake.

L.18: And it will be [that] the one fleeing from the sound of the terror will fall into the pit, \q and the one coming up from the midst of the pit will be caught in the snare; \q for windows from on high have been opened, \q and [the] foundations of [the] earth have shaken.

R.18: Anyone who runs away from the sounds of terror will fall into the pit. \q Anyone who climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. \q Windows in the sky have opened to pour down water, \q and the earth shakes down to its foundations.

decisions.choice: whoever flees ... falls into the pit ... is caught in the snare: no escape
decisions.reason: Escaping one danger only leads into the next, as in Amos 5:19, where one flees a lion and meets a bear.

decisions.choice: windows from on high have been opened: a flood like Noah's
decisions.reason: The words recall the flood, when "the windows of the heavens were opened" (Genesis 7:11; 8:2). With the broken covenant of verse 5, the judgment is pictured as an undoing of the world.

decisions.choice: to pour down water
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the sky's windows, which in Genesis 7:11 let down the flood rain.

records.source: רֹ֥עָה הִֽתְרֹעֲעָ֖ה הָאָ֑רֶץ פּ֤וֹר הִֽתְפּוֹרְרָה֙ אֶ֔רֶץ מ֥וֹט הִֽתְמוֹטְטָ֖ה אָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Utterly it has been broken, the earth; utterly it has been split, [the] earth; utterly it has been shaken, [the] earth.
pieces: The earth is shattered to pieces; \q the earth is torn right through; \q the earth reels and shudders.

L.19: Utterly broken is the earth; \q utterly split apart is [the] earth; \q utterly shaken is [the] earth.

R.19: The earth breaks into pieces. \q The earth splits wide open. \q The earth shakes violently.

decisions.choice: utterly broken ... split ... shaken: three doubled verbs
decisions.reason: As in verse 3, each verb is doubled for emphasis. The three verbs sound alike and build the picture of a great earthquake.

records.source: נ֣וֹעַ תָּנ֤וּעַ אֶ֨רֶץ֙ כַּשִּׁכּ֔וֹר וְהִֽתְנוֹדְדָ֖ה כַּמְּלוּנָ֑ה וְכָבַ֤ד עָלֶ֨יהָ֙ פִּשְׁעָ֔הּ וְנָפְלָ֖ה וְלֹא־תֹסִ֥יף קֽוּם׃ס
records.gloss: Wildly it will stagger, [the] earth, like the drunkard, and it will sway like the hut, and it will be heavy upon it, its rebellion, and it will fall and not will it again rise.
pieces: The earth will lurch to and fro like a drunk; \q it will rock like a watchman's shelter. \q Its rebellion will weigh it down; \q it will fall and not get up again.

L.20: The earth will stagger, stagger like the drunkard, \q and it will sway like the hut; \q and its rebellion will be heavy upon it, \q and it will fall and will not rise again.

R.20: The earth will stumble around like someone who is drunk. \q It will sway back and forth like a little shelter in a field. \q Its rebellion will be so heavy on it that it will fall down and never get up again.

decisions.choice: hut: a flimsy shelter for a watchman in a field
decisions.reason: The word names a light shelter put up for someone guarding a crop at night (1:8). In a storm it sways and falls.

decisions.choice: rebellion: breaking faith with God
decisions.reason: The word means revolt against a rightful ruler, as Israel's children "rebelled" against God in 1:2. Its weight is what brings the earth down.

decisions.choice: it will fall and not rise again: a final fall
decisions.reason: Amos 5:2 laments Israel in the same words: fallen, never to rise again.

decisions.choice: a watchman's shelter (Balanced); a little shelter in a field (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Hut" alone would not show why it sways; the word names a field-watchman's shelter.

records.source: וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יִפְקֹ֧ד יְהוָ֛ה עַל־צְבָ֥א הַמָּר֖וֹם בַּמָּר֑וֹם וְעַל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה עַל־הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will be in that day, he will visit, Yahweh, upon the host of the height in the height, and upon the kings of the ground upon the ground.
pieces: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will call to account the army of the heights up on high \q and the kings of the earth down on the earth.

L.21: And it will be in that day \q [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will visit [judgment] upon the host of the height in the height, \q and upon the kings of the ground upon the ground.

R.21: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will punish the powers of the sky, high above, \q and the kings who rule the earth, here below.

decisions.choice: visit upon: punish, call to account
decisions.reason: To "visit upon" someone is to come and deal with their wrongs (10:12; 13:11).

decisions.choice: the host of the height: the powers of the heavens
decisions.reason: The host of heaven is the stars and the heavenly beings, which other nations worshiped (Deuteronomy 4:19; 2 Kings 21:5). Scripture also speaks of powers on high behind the kingdoms of earth (Daniel 10:13, 20). God judges both the powers above and the kings below.

decisions.choice: the army of the heights (Balanced); the powers of the sky (Readable); "earth" for the ground
decisions.reason: The word for host is the one for an army, as in "the LORD of hosts". Readable says "powers" because these are ruling beings, not soldiers.

records.heading: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will reign on Mount Zion

records.source: וְאֻסְּפ֨וּ אֲסֵפָ֤ה אַסִּיר֙ עַל־בּ֔וֹר וְסֻגְּר֖וּ עַל־מַסְגֵּ֑ר וּמֵרֹ֥ב יָמִ֖ים יִפָּקֵֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: And they will be gathered, a gathering of prisoner[s] into a pit, and they will be shut up in a prison, and after many days they will be visited.
pieces: They will be rounded up as prisoners are, into a pit, \q and locked away in a prison; \q after many days they will be brought to judgment.

L.22: And they will be gathered [as] a gathering of prisoners into a pit, \q and they will be shut up in a prison, \q and after many days they will be visited.

R.22: They will be gathered together like prisoners and thrown into a deep pit. \q They will be locked up in a prison. \q After a long time, they will receive their punishment.

decisions.choice: they will be visited: they will be punished
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in verse 21. Here it most likely means the final punishment after a time of imprisonment. It can also mean to visit with favor, which would mean release after many days.

decisions.choice: a pit: a cistern used as a prison
decisions.reason: Dry cisterns served as dungeons (Genesis 37:24; Jeremiah 38:6). The pit also suggests the world of the dead (14:15).

decisions.choice: shut up in a prison ... after many days: imprisonment before final judgment
decisions.reason: Revelation 20:1-3, 7-10 uses a similar pattern: the enemy is bound and locked away, then dealt with after a long time.

records.source: וְחָֽפְרָה֙ הַלְּבָנָ֔ה וּבוֹשָׁ֖ה הַֽחַמָּ֑ה כִּֽי־מָלַ֞ךְ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת בְּהַ֤ר צִיּוֹן֙ וּבִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְנֶ֥גֶד זְקֵנָ֖יו כָּבֽוֹד׃פ
records.gloss: And it will be abashed, the moon, and it will be ashamed, the sun, for he will reign, Yahweh of hosts, on [the] mountain of Zion and in Jerusalem, and before his elders [will be] glory.
pieces: The moon will blush and the sun will hang its head, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will reign as king on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, \q and before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} elders there will be glory.

L.23: And the moon will be abashed, and the sun will be ashamed, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, \q and before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} elders [will be] glory.

R.23: The moon and the sun will seem to be ashamed, \q because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies will rule as king on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem. \q The leaders of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people will see {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

decisions.choice: the moon ... the sun: their light fades before God's glory
decisions.reason: The words used are poetic names, "the white one" and "the hot one" (also 30:26). The lights once worshiped as part of the host of heaven (verse 21) are put to shame by God's glory (60:19-20).

decisions.choice: will reign: has become king
decisions.reason: The verb form can mean that the LORD has taken up his reign, as in the cry "Yahweh reigns" (Psalm 93:1; 52:7). Here it looks to the day of judgment.

decisions.choice: before his elders, glory: as at Sinai
decisions.reason: At Sinai the elders of Israel saw God and his glory rested on the mountain (Exodus 24:9-11, 16-17). The scene is renewed on Mount Zion.

decisions.choice: will seem to be ashamed; the leaders of his people will see his glory
decisions.reason: Readable marks the shame of the sun and moon as a picture and explains "his elders" as the leaders of God's people.
